{{Short description|Italian inorganic chemist and academic (1930–2017)}}
{{notability|academic|date=May 2024}}
'''Lidia Vallarino''' (1930–2017) was an [[inorganic chemist]] who was chemistry lecturer at the University of Milan. In the 1950s and 19960s, she was a rare example of a well-published female active in [[coordination chemistry]] and [[organometallic chemistry]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://vcu.academicworks.com/donors/lidia-vallarino|title=Lidia Vallarino}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Lidia Vallarino Quagliano 1930 - 2017 |url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/name/quagliano/lidia}}</ref>

Vallarino received her PhD in 1954 from the University of Milan under the supervision of L. Malatesta for work on [[isocyanide complex]]es.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1039/jr9560001867 |title=366. IsoCyano-complexes of rhodium. Part I. Tetraisocyanorhodium(I) salts |date=1956 |last1=Malatesta |first1=L. |last2=Vallarino |first2=L. |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society (Resumed) |page=1867 }}</ref> She later took a position at ICI Laboratories under [[Joseph Chatt]], where she worked on [[diene complex]]es of the [[platinum group metal]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1039/JR9570002496 |title=Olefin Co-ordination Compounds. Part IV. Diene Complexes of Platinum(II). The Structure of Hofmann and von Narbutt's &#91;dicyclopentadiene(RO)PtCl&#93; |date=1957 |last1=Chatt |first1=J. |last2=Vallarino |first2=(Miss) L. M. |last3=Venanzi |first3=L. M. |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society (Resumed) |page=2496 }}</ref> As an independent scientist, she worked on both [[organorhodium chemistry]]<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1021/ic50024a007 |title=Preparation and Properties of a Series of Halocarbonylrhodates |date=1965 |last1=Vallarino |first1=L. M. |journal=Inorganic Chemistry |volume=4 |issue=2 |pages=161–165 }}</ref> and [[macrocyclic ligand|macrocyclic complex]]es
of the lanthanides.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1021/ic00230a042 |title=Hexaaza Macrocyclic Complexes of the Lanthanides |date=1986 |last1=De Cola |first1=L. |last2=Smailes |first2=D. L. |last3=Vallarino |first3=L. M. |journal=Inorganic Chemistry |volume=25 |issue=10 |pages=1729–1732 }}</ref>  She retired as professor of chemistry at [[Virginia Commonwealth University]].
